steps.surface: Settings → Model Providers → Local models, and the new-session form
steps.path: The engine card, the Recommended and Installed model lists, a model's Settings dialog, and the memory warning before a model loads
steps.headline: This is what done means.

rows.statement: When AMD's ROCm software is missing on Linux, the app shows the install command and types it into its own terminal for you to run.
rows.note: only half-related, but this makes me think we should add a simple "Terminal" entry to the provider list when creating a new session, and allow users to have just a bare terminal window as a "youcoded" session. this would ingratiate us with devs and we could have this change paste the command into a new terminal session.

rows.statement: Each downloaded model can set its own context length, Keep loaded, GPU layers, and a free-text box of extra engine flags.
rows.note: but, to be clear, the ui should still prioritize non-developers. things that would confuse people should be hidden by and "advanced settings" menu or something of the like, with (i) explainers for concepts

rows.statement: A model that can see images always downloads its vision file; there is no switch to skip it.
rows.note: how do others like unsloth studio handle this? i lean towards always download, but am open to providing an option if we REALLY feel like this may bother users

rows.statement: Speculative decoding and Compress context memory are visible switches under Advanced on the engine card, both on by default.
rows.note: fine with this being in advanced, along with some earlier settings. we should set the best defaults (like speculative decoding should probably default to "on").

rows.statement: A faster-engine button appears only for the matching graphics chip; you never land on a processor-only engine labelled CUDA or ROCm.
Choosing the CUDA engine always brings its runtime files along; there is no separate second download to remember.
On a shared-memory machine, the fit verdict counts the graphics pool limit and the memory available right now.
On a 'tight' or 'too large' verdict, the size bubble ends with 'Lower this model's context length in its Settings to shrink this.'
The before-load warning is asked once per model at a given context length and remembers your answer on this computer.
Adding vision downloads the file and moves the model into its own folder in one step; nothing on disk is rearranged otherwise.
Models whose family has no vision file show nothing new on their row.
While the engine runs, the card shows the chip in use, GB of models loaded, and the last reply's read and write speed, live.
The engine card is a title with its state, one fact line, a faster-engine row when your chip has one, and an Advanced row.
Set up shows one sentence, the command with Copy beside it, then Run in terminal and Check again — nothing else.
The switch is offered only once the app finds both the chip and its software; a failure after install shows the engine's own message.
On a Linux flavour the app cannot recognise, the box offers AMD's guide and Check again instead of a command.
Advanced opens in place: two speed switches with one-line hints, the context length, and one read-only row for version, backend and models folder.
Every on/off setting on these screens is the app's standard toggle row, never a hand-drawn one.
rows.threshold: the named test passes — no toggle anywhere in the desktop renderer sits outside a standard settings row

rows.statement: Changing a speed switch restarts the engine; a model in use reloads on its next message.
A model's size is one dotted number; hover or tap opens a small table of model file, download total and memory while running.
rows.note: can't tell if its a deck bug but this is not really visible or positioned properly. bad boy :(

rows.statement: The size breakdown bubble opens below the number, lined up with its left edge, and stays inside the dialog.
An eye marks a downloaded model that sees images and a page marks text-only; hovering either names it.
Under a model that could see, 'Add vision (0.9 GB)' is a short link and its hover points to it.
A model's Settings button opens a small dialog of its own, 'Model settings' with the model's name; the Installed list is unchanged.
Context length and Keep loaded are plain rows; Advanced unfolds Layers on graphics chip and Extra engine flags, each with an (i).
A mistyped extra flag stops only that model from loading and shows the engine's own message in its settings.
The memory warning is an expandable row: one amber sentence with a chevron that opens to the numbers line and the toggle row.
rows.note: put the "warn me about this" as a sub-card inside the expanded "model may not fit card". then this is good.

rows.statement: Open, the row's second line is the model size plus its context memory and what is already loaded — one line, no paragraph.
Open, the 'Warn me about this model' toggle is nested inside the warning card as its own small card, indented and tinted.
rows.note: put the "warn me about this" as a sub-card inside the expanded "model may not fit card". then this is good.

rows.statement: Closed, the warning is one amber line, and on Halftone and Meadow it still reads as a warning against the theme.
A too-large model shows the same row in the danger colour and opens to the numbers line only — no 'Warn me' toggle.
The size bubble lists 'Vision file (sees images)' as its own line, between Model file and Download, only for models that have one.
